The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in F.I.R./Case Crime No.42/2021, under Sections 406, 420, 504 and 506 I.P.C., Police Station Wazirganj, District Lucknow.

The prosecution case in brief is that the opposite party no.2 had lodged a first information report against the applicant and Smt. sentences.text: Few days' later, co-accused started demanding money in lieu of agreement to sale from the opposite party No.2 and the opposite party No.2 paid Rs.15,00,000/- total via cash and cheque on different dates to co-accused.

On 04.12.2020, the opposite party No.2 received a call from the applicant on his mobile number and the applicant told him that forget about the house for which you have entered into an agreement to sale with co-accused and started abusing him with caustic words.

When the applicant inquired about this incident with co-accused, she also refused to execute a sale deed in favour of opposite party No.2 despite the fact that the opposite party No.2 has paid Rs.15,00,000/- in total to the accused persons.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to rivalry and only with the intention to defame the image of the applicant and his entire family in the society.

He further submits that the applicant is neither seller, purchaser and marginal witness nor he received any money relating to the alleged sale agreement and he has also not received any amount either from the complainant or any one else with regard to house in question.

He further submits that earlier the applicant has filed an Application U/S 482 No.3976 of 2022, Smt. Poonam and Another vs. State of U.P. & Another and after hearing the matter, the Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 27.06.2022 disposed of the said application granting benefit of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Satendra Kumar Antil vs.
Central Bureau of Investigation and Another (Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.5191 of 2021 decided on 07.10.2021.

sentences.text: He further submits that the alleged offences are punishable up to seven years and after service of notice under Section 41-A Cr.P.C., the applicant had fully co-operated in the investigation of case.
He further submits that the applicant will not induce and threat any person so as to dissuade him from disclosing any facts to the learned trial court.
He further submits that the applicant is a permanent resident of District Lucknow and there is no chance of him absconding.
Several other submissions in order to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against the applicant have also been placed forth before the Court.
The circumstances which, according to the counsel, led to the false implication of the accused have also been touched upon at length.

It has been assured on behalf of the applicant that he is ready to cooperate with the process of law and shall faithfully make himself available before the court whenever required and is also ready to accept all the conditions which the Court may deem fit to impose upon him.

It has also been pointed out that the accused is not having any criminal history and in the wake of heavy pendency of cases in the Court, there is no likelihood of any early conclusion of trial.
Learned A.G.A. for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submits that the applicant has committed an heinous offence, as such, he is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.
